title: Graceful Shutdown and Signal Handling
description: Introduce built‑in graceful shutdown to ensure yantraverse stops accepting new requests on SIGTERM/SIGINT, drains existing connections, and exits cleanly. This improves reliability during deployments and prevents request loss.
testCases: Verify that on SIGTERM the server stops accepting new connections and returns 503 for subsequent requests
Confirm that in‑flight requests are allowed to complete before the process exits, with a timeout fallback
acceptance: When the process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, yantraverse must stop accepting new connections, respond with 503 to any new request, wait for all active requests to finish (up to a configurable timeout), log each shutdown step, and then exit with code 0. If the timeout expires, the process must force‑exit with code 1.
reason: Production deployments and container orchestrators require reliable shutdown to avoid dropped requests and data corruption. Adding this feature eliminates a common operational risk and aligns yantraverse with best‑practice Node.js server behavior.
